title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to otelsdk website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the otelsdk website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Hacks that get otelsdk building with brew protobuf on a Mac
description:
Hacks, do not merge, just use this to get unstuck

@schloerke and @jcheng5 you may still need to clone this PR and tweak the precise version of protobuf and abseil, but this got me and @schloerke a successful build of otelsdk on a Mac with brew protobuf

Using this hint:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/17258#issuecomment-2415135317

1. `brew install protobuf`, this should bring in `abseil` as well
2. Check `brew list protobuf` and look for `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/protobuf/29.3/include/`. If the versions are the same you should not have to change anything, otherwise tweak `Makevars.in`
3. Check `brew list abseil` and look for `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/abseil/20240722.1/include/`. If the versions are the same you should not have to change anything, otherwise tweak `Makevars.in`. Note that this reports `.../include/abseil` but you really just want up to `.../include/`
4. `devtools::load_all()` worked for me after that

title: New session API
description:
> OK, I have an idea that I think will work. It is essentially removing much of my extra session code and going back to what the C++ API is doing. Which means that we'd have a single context stack, but allow putting a (session) span on the context stack for the scope on an (R) function. So this is the API:
> 
> ```
> span <- start_span()
> sess <- start_session()
> with_session(sess, expr)
> local_session(sess)
> ```
> The only difference to the C++ API is that:
>
> * We'd activate new spans immediately.
> * We'd have "regular" spans and "session" spans. Regular spans end when they go out of scope, session spans don't.

Cf. https://github.com/r-lib/otelsdk/issues/24#issuecomment-2982788631

title: Improve the resource attributes we set for tracers by default
description:

I've also set up a reasonable set of default resources attributes (following the semantic conventions).

This fixes #11.

  outer <- trc$start_span("outer")
  outer$end()
